Engannim
ĕn-găn´nĭm
n. (spring of gardens; the name of two towns, one of them given to the Levites)
Hebrew eyn gannim, fountain of gardens — a name that describes what a spring makes of the ground around it.

Biblical Definition

One Engannim lies in the lowland of Judah: “And Zanoah, and Engannim, Tappuah, and Enam” (Josh 15:34). The other is in Issachar: “And Remeth, and Engannim, and Enhaddah, and Bethpazzez” (Josh 19:21), and it is set apart for the sons of Gershon: “Jarmuth with her suburbs, Engannim with her suburbs; four cities” (Josh 21:29). That allotment belongs to a larger arrangement: “All the cities of the Levites within the possession of the children of Israel were forty and eight cities with their suburbs” (Josh 21:41).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a garden as a piece of ground appropriated to the cultivation of herbs, fruits and flowers, and suburbs as the parts adjacent to a city.

expand to see more

GARDEN, n. A piece of ground appropriated to the cultivation of herbs, or plants, fruits and flowers.

SUBURB, n. A building without the walls of a city, but near them; more generally, the parts adjacent to a city or town.

LEVITE, n. One of the tribe or family of Levi; a descendant of Levi; more particularly, an officer in the Jewish church.

Key Scripture

Josh 15:34 — "And Zanoah, and Engannim, Tappuah, and Enam,"

Josh 19:21 — "And Remeth, and Engannim, and Enhaddah, and Bethpazzez;"

Josh 21:29 — "Jarmuth with her suburbs, Engannim with her suburbs; four cities."

Josh 21:41 — "All the cities of the Levites within the possession of the children of Israel were forty and eight cities with their suburbs."

Modern Corruption

Levi got no territory and forty-eight towns scattered through every other tribe, so that the teaching order lived where the people lived.

expand to see more

Joshua 21 completes a design begun in Genesis 49. Jacob had said of Simeon and Levi that he would divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel — spoken as a judgment for the violence at Shechem. In Levi's case the scattering became a vocation. The tribe received no block of land but forty-eight cities with their suburbs, distributed through every other inheritance, six of them cities of refuge. Deuteronomy 33:10 gives the purpose: they shall teach Jacob thy judgments, and Israel thy law. A curse became the mechanism by which every tribe had teachers of the law inside its own borders.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that God's ministers are meant to live among the people they teach. The Levitical cities were not a compound; they were forty-eight ordinary towns, each with pasture around it, in the middle of everyone else's inheritance. Malachi 2:7 states the office: the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth. And the LORD Himself was Levi's portion, which is the other half of the arrangement — a tribe with no estate, dependent on tithes and on God, teaching the tribes that had estates.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew ayin (H5869), spring; gan / gannim (H1588), garden, gardens; migrash (H4054), suburbs, common land around a city.

expand to see more

Hebrew ayin (H5869) — spring, fountain; Joshua 15:34, 19:21.

Hebrew gan (H1588) — garden; Genesis 2:8, Song of Solomon 4:12.

Hebrew migrash (H4054) — suburbs, open pasture land; Joshua 21:29, 21:41, Numbers 35:2.

Hebrew Gereshon (H1648) — Gershon, son of Levi; Joshua 21:27, Exodus 6:16.

Hebrew cheleq (H2506) — portion, share; Deuteronomy 10:9, Numbers 18:20.

Usage

"“Engannim with her suburbs; four cities” — a Levitical town in Issachar."

"“Forty and eight cities with their suburbs” — the whole Levitical portion."

"“Zanoah, and Engannim, Tappuah, and Enam” — the other town, in Judah."
